title: Email & calendar
blurb: Outlook, Apple Mail and webmail: not sending, not syncing, password prompts, calendar trouble.

remedies.title: Outlook isn't getting new email
remedies.why: Outlook is set to Work Offline, lost its connection, its sign-in expired, or the mailbox is full.

steps.text: Check the bottom of the Outlook window: if it says Working Offline or Disconnected, click Send/Receive › Work Offline to turn it off.
Sign in to Outlook on the web (outlook.office.com or your provider's webmail). If mail arrives there, the problem is Outlook on this computer.
Quit Outlook completely and reopen it; enter your password if asked.
Check the mailbox isn't full: File › Info › Mailbox settings shows the space used.
Check rules aren't moving mail away: File › Manage Rules & Alerts (or Outlook › Settings › Rules on Mac).
If none of that helps, make a new mail profile: Control Panel › Mail › Show Profiles › Add.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT whether Outlook on the web gets the mail; that tells them if it's the mailbox or this computer.

remedies.title: Outlook keeps asking for my password
remedies.why: A saved password is out of date after a change, or the modern sign-in token got damaged.

steps.text: If you changed your password recently, sign in with the new one everywhere, including your phone.
Remove old saved passwords: Credential Manager › Windows Credentials › delete entries starting with MicrosoftOffice or Outlook, then restart Outlook.
Delete old Outlook or Exchange entries in Keychain Access, then restart Outlook.
Sign out of Office and back in: File › Office Account › Sign out, close all Office apps, open Outlook and sign in.
For work accounts check "Access work or school" lists your account and isn't showing an error.

remedies.escalate: If it keeps asking after this, IT should check your account (it may be locked or need a new device registration).

remedies.title: Email stuck in the Outbox
remedies.why: The attachment is too big, Outlook is offline, or the message is open or damaged.

steps.text: Check you're online and Outlook isn't set to Work Offline.
Attachments over ~20–25 MB are refused by most mail servers: delete the message, and send a share link (OneDrive, iCloud, Dropbox) instead.
Open the Outbox, drag the stuck message to Drafts, open it and press Send again.
If it won't move, turn on Work Offline, then delete or move it, then go back online.

remedies.title: Attachment is too large to send
remedies.why: Mail servers limit message size, usually 20–35 MB total, and attachments grow by about a third when sent.

steps.text: Share a link instead: upload to OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud or Dropbox and insert the link.
In Outlook, attach as a cloud link: Attach file › choose the OneDrive copy › Share link.
On a Mac, Mail Drop sends large files through iCloud automatically when asked.
Zip several files into one, or shrink photos and PDFs before attaching.

remedies.title: "Mailbox is full" or almost full
remedies.why: The mailbox has reached its size limit; sent items, deleted items and large attachments are usually the cause.

steps.text: Empty Deleted Items and Junk.
Search for big messages: in Outlook search type size:huge or size:enormous (Windows), sort by size, delete or save the attachments elsewhere.
Clean Sent Items: old messages with attachments take the most space.
Ask IT about an archive mailbox if you need to keep everything.

remedies.escalate: IT can raise the limit or turn on online archiving.

remedies.title: Outlook is slow or freezes
remedies.why: A very large mailbox or data file, an add-in, or Outlook still downloading a lot of mail.

steps.text: Give it a few minutes after opening; it may be syncing (look at the bottom bar).
Start Outlook without add-ins: hold Ctrl while opening it and say Yes to safe mode. If it's fast, turn add-ins off one by one in File › Options › Add-ins.
Cut the mailbox size (see "Mailbox is full").
Repair Office: Settings › Apps › Microsoft 365 › Modify › Quick Repair.
Try the new Outlook (toggle at the top right) or Outlook on the web to see if it's this install.

remedies.title: Outlook search finds nothing or misses messages
remedies.why: Outlook search relies on the system's search index, which can be incomplete or damaged.

steps.text: Wait if Outlook was just set up; indexing can take hours. Outlook shows progress under Search › Search Tools › Indexing Status.
Rebuild the Windows search index.
Make sure Outlook isn't excluded from Spotlight: System Settings › Spotlight (and Privacy list).
Search Outlook on the web; it searches the server directly.

remedies.title: Emails go to Junk or my emails land in other people's spam
remedies.why: Filters guess wrong, or your messages look like spam (many links, attachments, or a domain set up without email checks).

steps.text: Mark wanted messages as Not Junk and add the sender to Safe Senders.
Ask people to check their spam and mark your mail as not spam.
Avoid all-caps subjects, many links, and large attachments to new contacts.
For your own domain, ask whoever runs it to check SPF, DKIM and DMARC records.

remedies.escalate: If many recipients get your mail as spam, IT should check your domain's email records and whether it's on a blocklist.

remedies.title: I got a suspicious email (or clicked a link in one)
remedies.why: Phishing emails pretend to be a bank, a delivery, Microsoft or your boss to get passwords or money.

steps.text: Don't reply, open attachments, or click links. Report it with the Report button in Outlook, or forward it to your IT team.
If you typed a password into the page, change that password now from a trusted device and turn on two-step sign-in.
If you opened an attachment, disconnect from the network and tell IT right away.
Requests for gift cards, bank changes or urgent payments: check by phone with the person, using a number you already have.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT immediately if you clicked, typed a password or opened an attachment; the faster, the less damage.

remedies.title: Calendar not syncing between computer and phone
remedies.why: The phone or computer uses a different account, sync is off, or a shared calendar isn't refreshing.

steps.text: Check the event on Outlook on the web (or iCloud.com / Google Calendar). Whichever device disagrees with the web is the one to fix.
On the phone, check the account's Calendars switch is on (iPhone: Settings › Calendar › Accounts).
Remove and re-add a shared calendar that's stuck.
In Outlook on Windows turn on "Turn on shared calendar improvements" in File › Account Settings › your account › Change › More Settings › Advanced.

remedies.title: Meetings show at the wrong time
remedies.why: The computer, phone or calendar has a different time zone set, or daylight saving was entered by hand.

steps.text: Set time and time zone automatically on this computer.
Set time and time zone automatically on this computer.
Check Outlook's own time zone: File › Options › Calendar › Time zones (Windows) or Outlook › Settings › Calendar (Mac).
Ask the organiser which time zone they used when creating the meeting.

remedies.title: Apple Mail won't send or receive
remedies.why: The account's sign-in expired, the account is offline, or its settings changed at the provider.

steps.text: In Mail choose Mailbox › Take All Accounts Online.
Window › Connection Doctor shows which account fails and why.
Re-enter the password in System Settings › Internet Accounts › the account.
For Gmail and Outlook.com accounts, remove and add the account again to sign in the modern way.

remedies.title: How do I set an out-of-office reply?
remedies.why: Automatic replies are set on the mail server, so they work even with the computer off.

steps.text: Outlook: File › Automatic Replies (Windows) or Tools › Out of Office (Mac). New Outlook / web: Settings › Mail › Automatic replies.
Set an end date so it switches itself off, and write a separate reply for people outside your organisation.
Gmail: Settings › See all settings › Vacation responder.

remedies.title: Shared mailbox doesn't show in Outlook
remedies.why: New access can take up to an hour to appear, and the new Outlook needs shared mailboxes added by hand.

steps.text: Restart Outlook; access given recently can take an hour to show.
Add it by hand: right-click your account › Add shared folder or mailbox, type its address.
Check it in Outlook on the web: your picture › Open another mailbox.

remedies.escalate: If it's not in Outlook on the web either, IT needs to give you access.
